_doc: Training data recipe — 'Broad Brain' mix v4 (Quality-pruned for small-model focus).
Goal: train a small model (17M–280M params) toward Claude-Code-ish capability
in code, math, reasoning, and conversational assistant work — while keeping
the 'Mindees' persona on top via --corpus and --distill-corpus weights.
• Removed 4 entries with kind='preference' / 'agentic' that the loader
silently skips (pretrain.py only handles 'raw' and 'dialogue'). They
live in _pending_stages below as placeholders for a future DPO/RLHF
stage that hasn't been built yet.
• Removed oasst1 — flat-tree storage format yields '0 conversations'
in the parser. Its tokens were noise rather than signal at any weight.
• Removed tulu3-sft-mixture — non-commercial subsets risk a license
violation on the public-revision HF model.
• Removed slim-orca and ultrachat — heavy redundancy with openhermes +
smoltalk for broad chat. At small scale, three datasets covering the
same ground just means more epochs over the same patterns.
• Lowered token caps on the big synthetic mixes so no single dataset
dominates several epochs before others finish one.
• Rebalanced weights with explicit tiers (anchor / broad / code / math /
1.8  persona protection / code crown: systemchat, magicoder-evol
1.5  broad chat / math / code instructions: openhermes, metamath,
TOTAL POOL ≈ 46M tokens. Scaling math for the two training environments:
→ cycles whole pool ~1.3× per day, ~9 epochs/week
home-11gb variant (local RTX / Kaggle / Colab, batch=2, seq=2048):
→ cycles whole pool ~0.4× per session, ~3 epochs across 8 sessions
All four environments train independently and push to separate HF branches.
main (local RTX) is sacrosanct — never touched by CI or notebooks.
The Mindees persona is layered on top via --corpus + --distill-corpus
weighted at 1.0 + 4.0 respectively in pretrain.py invocations. Those
signals override anything in this mix when prompts match persona triggers.
This mix supplies general capability; persona is the corpus layer above it.

_pending_stages._doc: Datasets staged for a future DPO/RLHF training pipeline that hasn't been built yet. The current pretrain.py loader handles only kind='raw' and kind='dialogue' — anything else is silently skipped. When a separate dpo_train.py exists, wire these into its config.

sources.name: dolly
sources.note: ANCHOR. Human-written instructions + responses. Zero synthetic noise.

sources.name: no-robots
sources.note: ANCHOR. 10K examples human-curated by skilled annotators. Highest instruction quality per token in the entire mix.

sources.name: smol-smoltalk
sources.note: ANCHOR. HuggingFace's instruction-tuning dataset *adapted specifically for sub-1B models*. Best structural fit for cpu_max_5h_50k (17M) and home-11gb (280M).

sources.name: systemchat
sources.note: PERSONA PROTECTION. Multi-turn dialogues with diverse system prompts. Teaches the model to follow CUSTOM personas cleanly — directly counter-acts the default 'as an AI' robotic register that synthetic SFT mixes drift toward.

sources.name: openhermes
sources.note: BROAD CHAT. 1M+ instruction examples — sales, marketing, psychology, business, motivation, fitness, wealth all show up organically. Synthetic (GPT-distilled) but highest-quality broad chat dataset on HF.

sources.name: smoltalk
sources.note: BROAD CHAT. Synthetic SFT dataset used for SmolLM2-Instruct. Broad instruction-following and conversational coverage.

sources.name: wizardlm-evol
sources.note: BROAD CHAT. 196k evolved instructions — adds a different synthetic *distribution* from openhermes (Wizard evol-instruct prompting vs. OpenHermes Orca-lineage), reducing redundancy.

sources.name: magicoder-evol
sources.note: CODE CROWN. 110K evolved code instructions. Highest-quality code SFT on HF — primary driver of Claude-Code-ish capability at this scale.

sources.name: codefeedback-filtered
sources.note: CODE. Filtered high-quality code instruction data. Complementary distribution to magicoder + code-alpaca.

sources.name: code-alpaca
sources.note: CODE. Code instructions in alpaca format — simpler-task distribution than magicoder.

sources.name: opencoder-sft-stage2
sources.note: CODE. Educational code instructions + test-case-oriented examples. Backstop in case The Stack downloads get gated.

sources.name: the-stack-python
sources.note: CODE RAW. Real Python from public GitHub — production patterns that don't appear in synthetic instruction data.

sources.name: the-stack-typescript
sources.note: CODE RAW. TypeScript — Next.js / React / web stack vocabulary.

sources.name: the-stack-javascript
sources.note: CODE RAW. JavaScript — JSX patterns, React Native components, Node.js.

sources.name: metamath
sources.note: MATH. 395K math problems with worked chain-of-thought. Primary math signal.

sources.name: mathinstruct
sources.note: MATH. Hybrid CoT + program-of-thought math instructions. Complements MetaMath with PoT distribution.

sources.name: open-platypus
sources.note: REASONING. STEM reasoning, logic, science. Curated from many sources.

sources.name: ultrainteract
sources.note: REASONING. Tree-structured CoT reasoning. Strong on real-world problem solving.

sources.name: openthoughts2
sources.note: REASONING. Synthetic reasoning across math/science/code/puzzles. Kept low-weight at small scale — capacity for explicit reasoning is limited below ~280M params.

sources.name: the-stack-solidity
sources.note: DOMAIN SPICE. Solidity smart contracts. Web3 / blockchain code vocabulary.

sources.name: the-stack-html
sources.note: DOMAIN SPICE. HTML markup. Visual-structure vocabulary for UI tasks.

sources.name: the-stack-css
sources.note: DOMAIN SPICE. CSS / SCSS. Tailwind-adjacent class vocabulary for UI/UX.

sources.name: empathetic-counseling
sources.note: EMPATHY. Counseling-style dialogue. Adds emotional awareness and supportive tone. Low weight to avoid making the model sound therapist-like on non-emotional turns.

sources.name: mental-health-counseling
sources.note: EMPATHY. Counseling Q&A data for sensitive-response behavior. Lowest weight — used as a floor for emotional turns, not a default.

sources.name: tinystories
sources.note: WARMUP. Narrative warmup — helps embeddings stabilise early in training. Cap is intentionally low; the model doesn't need to specialize in children's stories.

sources.name: fineweb-edu
sources.note: KNOWLEDGE. High-quality educational web text. Adds factual / explanatory knowledge without relying only on chat data. Capped at 3M (full FW-Edu is 1.3 trillion tokens — would dominate).
